I must strongly object to the conclusion of "Cholecystitis." Our entire discussion has centered on a pregnant patient with abdominal pain and vaginal bleeding. The symptoms of shoulder pain (referred pain from hemoperitoneum) and dizziness (hypovolemia) are classic signs of a ruptured ectopic pregnancy, not a gallbladder issue. While cholecystitis can cause right upper quadrant pain and sometimes shoulder tip pain, it does not explain the vaginal bleeding in the context of pregnancy, nor does it account for the specific triad of symptoms we are worried about. Diagnosing cholecystitis here would be a catastrophic error that ignores the primary complaint of vaginal bleeding.
